fullPassage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that, in a changing environment, it is not clear that consistency is always a virtue and that one of the advantages of human judgment is the ability to detect change. Thus, in changing environments, it might be advantageous to combine human judgment and statistical models. Blattberg and Hoch examined this possibility by having supermarket managers forecast demand for certain products and then creating a composite forecast by averaging these judgments with the forecasts of statistical models based on past data. The logic was that statistical models deny stable conditions and therefore cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events such as actions taken by competitors or the introduction of new products. Humans, however, can incorporate these novel factors in their judgments. The composite — or average of human judgments and statistical models — proved to be more accurate than either the statistical models or the managers working alone.

[ of / demand / for / novel / on / account / effects / cannot / the / events ]

det.korean: 새로운 사건이 수요에 미치는 영향을 설명할 수 없다.
det.analysis: 원문: cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events
det.tip: account for = 설명하다. effects on demand = 수요에 미치는 영향

questions.wa: cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events
accept: cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events

questions.passage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that, in a changing environment, it is not clear that consistency is always a virtue and that one of the advantages of human judgment is the ability to detect change. Thus, in changing environments, it might be advantageous to __________. Blattberg and Hoch examined this possibility by having supermarket managers forecast demand for certain products and then creating a composite forecast by averaging these judgments with the forecasts of statistical models based on past data. The logic was that statistical models deny stable conditions and therefore cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events such as actions taken by competitors or the introduction of new products. Humans, however, can incorporate these novel factors in their judgments. The composite — or average of human judgments and statistical models — proved to be more accurate than either the statistical models or the managers working alone.
